text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Two German parliamentarians arrive in Hanoi today to hold talks with the Justice, Interior and Labour ministries to get first-hand information on recent law reforms.
-- There are nearly one million blind people across Vietnam, according to the National Institute of Ophthalmology.
-- Ho Chi Minh City authorities are considering a project to build a 25-kilometre (15-mile) metro system connecting city districts with suburban areas. The costs are estimated at $218 million.
-- The Ministry of Finance has drafted a document aimed at offering more attractive land rentals in cases where investment needs to be promoted.

-- Economic cooperation and regional peace will be two key issues which the Association of Southeast Asian Nations will pay attention to in the next century, Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong has said.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet will pay a three-day official visit to Laos starting from August 12.
-- The laws and rights of the Vietnamese people will be ineffective without a strong state system, Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has told party members.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has welcomed financial cooperation with Laos during talks with the Laotian Finance Minister Saysomphone Phomvihane.
-- Hanoi celebrated the 30th anniversary of the Association of South-East Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Thursday.
-- Ho Chi Minh City is making comprehensive checks on all legal documents to identify contradictions, and documents issued with inappropriate authorisation.
